name: walmsley2024_spray_dryer
description: Milk powder spray dryer (main air chamber, static and vibrating fluid beds, exhaust air with heat recovery). Loads in kW. Table 1 data as published.
reference: Walmsley, Lincoln, Padullés, Cleland (2024), Energies 17, 2838, Table 1 (case first presented by Liang et al.).

provenance.stream data: published (Table 1). WARNING: Table 1 is inconsistent with the paper's own targets (4.98 / 3.99 MW) by the first law; see verify_walmsley2024.py
provenance.source_T_C: assumed: 15 °C (dead state), where the cooled exhaust air ends
provenance.sink levels: assumed, illustrative: 120 °C (fluid beds) and 200 °C (upper end of IEA HPT Annex 58 scope); the main air chamber up to 236 °C stays on fired heating
provenance.economics: assumed: no economic data in the source (see economics.sources)
provenance.film coefficients: none: the streams are mostly air, and Stampfli et al. (2018) give no air coefficients; enter your own values for supertargeting

economics._note: No economic data in the source. Prices: Eurostat Portugal 2026-S1 for the site's consumption band at 8000 h/year; heat pump investment: Danish Energy Agency catalogue by sink temperature with its lift and steam add-ons; other parameters: tool defaults (Sources page). All are assumptions for this case.

hp_dea_1_1.source: Danish Energy Agency, Technology Data - Industrial Process Heat (2025), 'Nominal investment (*total)' 2025, equipment + installation, per MW of heat output, sheet 1.1 'Heat pump, up to 60 °C, temp. lift 40 K': 0.95 M€/MW (0.91-0.95), unit size 0.5-5 MW

hp_dea_2a.source: Danish Energy Agency, Technology Data - Industrial Process Heat (2025), 'Nominal investment (*total)' 2025, equipment + installation, per MW of heat output, sheet 2.a 'High-temperature heat pumps up to 125 °C': 1.2 M€/MW (0.9-1.5), unit size 0.3-25 MW

hp_dea_2b.source: Danish Energy Agency, Technology Data - Industrial Process Heat (2025), 'Nominal investment (*total)' 2025, equipment + installation, per MW of heat output, sheet 2.b 'High-temperature heat pumps up to 150 °C': 1.55 M€/MW (1.25-1.8), unit size 0.5-80 MW. No catalogue sheet above 150 °C: units with hotter sinks are costed with this sheet as an extrapolation (flagged)

dea_lift_2a.source: Danish Energy Agency, Technology Data - Industrial Process Heat (2025), 2025 values, sheet 2.a: 'Additional equipment cost for temperature lift above 75 K' 0.15 M€/MW (0.05-0.25)

dea_lift_2b.source: Danish Energy Agency, Technology Data - Industrial Process Heat (2025), 2025 values, sheet 2.b: 'Additional equipment cost for temperature lift above 75 K' 0.2 M€/MW (0.1-0.3)

dea_steam.source: Danish Energy Agency, Technology Data - Industrial Process Heat (2025), 2025 values, sheets 2.a and 2.b: 'Steam generation increases equipment cost by' 0.2 M€/MW (0.05-0.3); applied to isothermal sinks (steam). The sheets' COP penalty for steam (-0.15) is not applied: COP comes from the Lorenz model

sources.prices: Eurostat nrg_pc_203 (gas) and nrg_pc_205 (electricity), Portugal, 2026-S1, excluding VAT and other recoverable taxes and levies, EUR/kWh, gas on GCV (data/sources/eurostat_portugal_prices.csv). The plant is not in Portugal: these prices place it in the dissertation's context. Bands: gas I3 0.0512, I4 0.0445, I5 0.0420; electricity ID 0.1135, IE 0.0897, IF 0.0789. Band check at 8000 h/year: plant size not published; estimated 8.3 t/h powder from the case's air heating (6.03 MW) and the specific air-heater use of Walmsley et al. (2016), 'Total Site Utility Systems Optimisation for Milk Powder Production', CET 52, 235-240, DOI 10.3303/CET1652040: 30 t/h milk powder plant, electricity 210-220 kWh/t powder (literature 150-400), fuel 5,200 MJ/t powder (base case) (2,610 MJ/t). Gas about 5.2 GJ/t x 8.3 x 8000 = 0.35 million GJ (I4); electricity 220 kWh/t x 8.3 x 8000 = 14.6 GWh + heat pumps 19.6 GWh = 34 GWh (IE)
sources.heat_pump_cost: Danish Energy Agency catalogue (2025) by sink temperature, linear in capacity, plus the catalogue's add-ons for lift above 75 K (sink outlet minus source outlet) and steam generation (isothermal sinks). Replaces Padullés et al. (2026, Table 3), which is fitted to brewery heat pumps and gives 0.75-0.88 M€/MW for 2-3 MW units, below the catalogue range 0.9-1.5 M€/MW for sinks up to 125 °C. Indirect cost of new hot-water piping (0.23 M€/MW, 'relevant when needing to install new hot water piping instead of existing steam piping') is a scenario, not in the base

hp_dea_1_1.source: Danish Energy Agency, Technology Data - Industrial Process Heat (2025), 'Nominal investment (*total)' 2025, equipment + installation, per MW of heat output, sheet 1.1 'Heat pump, up to 60 °C, temp. lift 40 K': 0.95 M€/MW (0.91-0.95), unit size 0.5-5 MW + 0.19 M€/MW indirect (sheet 1.1)

hp_dea_2a.source: Danish Energy Agency, Technology Data - Industrial Process Heat (2025), 'Nominal investment (*total)' 2025, equipment + installation, per MW of heat output, sheet 2.a 'High-temperature heat pumps up to 125 °C': 1.2 M€/MW (0.9-1.5), unit size 0.3-25 MW + 0.23 M€/MW indirect (new hot-water piping)

hp_dea_2b.source: Danish Energy Agency, Technology Data - Industrial Process Heat (2025), 'Nominal investment (*total)' 2025, equipment + installation, per MW of heat output, sheet 2.b 'High-temperature heat pumps up to 150 °C': 1.55 M€/MW (1.25-1.8), unit size 0.5-80 MW. No catalogue sheet above 150 °C: units with hotter sinks are costed with this sheet as an extrapolation (flagged) + 0.23 M€/MW indirect (new hot-water piping)

dea_lift_2a.source: Danish Energy Agency, Technology Data - Industrial Process Heat (2025), 2025 values, sheet 2.a: 'Additional equipment cost for temperature lift above 75 K' 0.15 M€/MW (0.05-0.25)

dea_lift_2b.source: Danish Energy Agency, Technology Data - Industrial Process Heat (2025), 2025 values, sheet 2.b: 'Additional equipment cost for temperature lift above 75 K' 0.2 M€/MW (0.1-0.3)

dea_steam.source: Danish Energy Agency, Technology Data - Industrial Process Heat (2025), 2025 values, sheets 2.a and 2.b: 'Steam generation increases equipment cost by' 0.2 M€/MW (0.05-0.3); applied to isothermal sinks (steam). The sheets' COP penalty for steam (-0.15) is not applied: COP comes from the Lorenz model

basis_hint: No operating hours are published for this plant. Milk supply varies considerably during the year (Atkins et al., 2009), so New Zealand milk-powder plants do not run all year: 8000 h/year is an upper bound. Price bands assume a plant of about 8.3 t/h powder (estimated: case air heating 6.03 MW / 2,610 MJ/t, Walmsley et al., 2016); at 8000 h: gas I4 (0.0445 €/kWh), electricity IE (0.0897) once the heat pumps are added. Change the prices in step 6 if you change the hours.
